text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. Developers often refactor to make programs easier to read and understand. For example, they may rename variables, split large functions into smaller ones, or remove repeated code. The main goal is to keep the same behavior while making the code cleaner and simpler to maintain. Refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when quick fixes are used instead of proper solutions. Although refactoring takes time, it saves effort later and makes future changes safer and faster.
